title: Relative marked reversal, mapping objects and cartesian horns
statement:
Use simplicial sets, functor objects and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], marked simplicial sets, $K^\flat,K^\sharp$, marked products and model-category conventions of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], and the opposite $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-opposite-homotopy-calculus]. Extend the inner-fibration and cartesian/cocartesian edge horn definitions of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] to arbitrary simplicial bases: cartesian edges solve final-horn problems for every $n\geq2$ with prescribed edge $\{n-1,n\}$, and a cartesian fibration has cartesian lifts with prescribed target of every base edge; cocartesian means the initial-horn and prescribed-source conditions. No quasicategory hypothesis on total space or base is imposed. For a small base $S$ let $\mathsf M_S$ be the category of marked simplicial sets over $S$, and define $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_S(X,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf M_S}(X\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,Y)$. Put $O_S(X,M)=(X^{\mathrm{op}},M)$ over $S^{\mathrm{op}}$, retaining the same degree-one subset of marked edges. Then $O_S:\mathsf M_S\to\mathsf M_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}$ is an equivalence with inverse $O_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}$, preserving degreewise limits, colimits and monomorphisms. It exchanges cartesian and cocartesian fibrations, their natural markings and maps preserving their distinguished edges. There are natural isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}(O_SX,O_SY)\cong(\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_S(X,Y))^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad O_S(X\times K^\sharp)\cong O_SX\times(K^{\mathrm{op}})^\sharp.$$
These respect identities, composition, tensors and their right adjoint cotensors, and restrict to opposite isomorphisms on the full simplicial subsets of $\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(X,Y)$ spanned by distinguished-edge-preserving maps and on their cores. If $i\mathbin{\square}j$ denotes the pushout product of a marked map $i$ and an unmarked map $j:K\to L$, using tensor $X\times K^\sharp$, then $O_S(i\mathbin{\square}j)\cong O_S(i)\mathbin{\square}j^{\mathrm{op}}$. For every $a:T\to S$, composition $a_!$ and degreewise pullback $a^*$ satisfy $O_Sa_!\cong(a^{\mathrm{op}})_!O_T$ and $O_Ta^*\cong(a^{\mathrm{op}})^*O_S$, compatibly with their adjunction units and counits. The same reversal identifies vertex fibers with their opposites.
